newsitem.title: USA: Martin Luther King assassin Ray near death.
newsitem.headline: Martin Luther King assassin Ray near death.

text.p: James Earl Ray, the unrepentant assassin of black civil rights leader Martin Luther King Jr., was near death in a hospital on Tuesday suffering from liver failure, prison officials said.

"His condition is critical," said Jim Rose, assistant commissioner at the Tennessee State Corrections Department. Ray, 68, was brought to Columbia Memorial Hospital on Saturday from a prison hospital in West Nashville.

He was moved from his cell in Riverbend Maximum Security Prison near Nashville a month ago and has been ill for more than a year, prison officials said. They refused to describe Ray's specific illness, citing confidentiality laws.

Ray was sentenced to 99 years in prison for the April 4, 1968, shooting of King as the famed civil rights leader stood on the balcony of the Lorraine Hotel in Memphis. Police found a rifle and a shoddy rooming house where the shot was fired from a second-floor bathroom window but the gunman escaped.

Fingerprints on the rifle were traced to Ray, who was tracked to Atlanta, Toronto, London, Portugal and finally back to London, where he was arrested by Scotland Yard detectives on June 8. He confessed to the slaying and a trial was never held but he soon recanted and has repeatedly sought a full court hearing.
Ray said he bought the rifle in a sporting goods store for the real killer, a mystery accomplice he named as "Raoul."

Ever since King's slaying, which touched off weeks of race riots in cities across the nation, it became a favoured subject of conspiracy theorists, second only to interest in the assassination some five years earlier of President John Kennedy.

Rumours of a wider conspiracy against King were fed by a purported FBI campaign to undermine the outspoken black leader. There were also questions about how Ray managed to escape to Europe and whether he had backers.
